projects.name: Note Taker – Cross-Platform Desktop Note-Taking App
projects.description: A feature-rich desktop note-taking app built with React, Vite, and Electron, supporting rich text notes, todos with timers, day plans, and freehand diagrams — stored entirely on-device.

detail.overview: Note Taker is a cross-platform desktop app that unifies four note types — rich text notes, todo lists with countdown timers, structured day plans, and freehand diagrams — in a single local-first application built on Electron and React.
detail.problem: Most note-taking tools are cloud-dependent, fragmented across multiple apps, or lack the flexibility to handle different types of structured content (free text, tasks, daily planning, and visual diagrams) in one place.
detail.solution: Built a fully local Electron app where all data is stored as a JSON file on the user's machine via IPC, with a rich React UI featuring a TipTap-powered editor, Excalidraw for diagrams, and a slash command menu for fast content insertion.
features: Four note types: rich text Notes, Todos with per-item countdown timers, Day Plans with template sections, and Excalidraw-powered Diagrams
TipTap rich text editor with headings, tables, images, code blocks, task lists, and a slash command menu
Notebook, tag, category, color label, and favorites organization with sidebar filters
Six built-in themes (Default Light/Dark, Midnight, Sepia, Nord, Forest) with system preference sync
Fuzzy quick-open palette (⌘K), desktop reminders via Electron, and export to Markdown or HTML
Configurable local JSON storage with auto-save (800 ms debounce) and storage migration from Settings
detail.challenges: Integrating Excalidraw and TipTap within Electron's renderer process while keeping auto-save performant, and wiring Electron IPC for file I/O and native desktop notifications without blocking the UI thread.
detail.outcome: A fully offline, privacy-first desktop note app that ships as a native binary for macOS, Windows, and Linux via electron-builder.

projects.name: Orchestrator – LLM Inference Benchmarking Framework
projects.description: An internal orchestration framework to benchmark a custom vLLM-based inference engine across parallelism strategies and GPU configurations.

detail.overview: Orchestrator is a benchmarking and testing framework built to evaluate tLLM (a custom vLLM-based inference engine) across a wide range of configurations on multi-node GPU clusters including H200 ×8, A100 ×4, and RTX 4090 ×4.
detail.problem: Evaluating LLM serving performance across different parallelism strategies, hardware setups, and optimization techniques (KV-caching, dynamic batching, CUDA graphs) was a manual, time-consuming, and error-prone process.
detail.solution: Built a framework that automates benchmark runs across configurations, uses Docker containers with GPU slicing for parallel test execution on a single machine, and manages process scheduling via SLURM.
features: Supports Pipeline, Data, and Expert Parallelism configurations
Benchmarks KV-caching, dynamic batching, and CUDA graph optimizations
Parallel test execution via Docker GPU slicing
Process allocation and scheduling managed with SLURM
Runs across H200, A100, and RTX 4090 multi-node clusters
detail.challenges: Coordinating parallel benchmark runs across heterogeneous GPU hardware while isolating test configurations cleanly required careful orchestration of Docker containers and SLURM job scheduling.
detail.outcome: Enabled rapid, reproducible evaluation of LLM engine configurations in a production-grade environment, directly informing infrastructure decisions.

projects.name: IPAuthor – OfficeAction Patent Drafting Platform
projects.description: An end-to-end AI patent drafting tool using LiteLLM, OpenAI fine-tuning, Gemini, and RAG, deployed on AWS.

detail.overview: IPAuthor is an AI-powered platform that automates the drafting of patent OfficeAction responses, combining LLM fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation, and a production-grade cloud backend.
detail.problem: Drafting patent OfficeAction responses is a highly specialized, time-consuming process that typically requires significant attorney involvement, making it expensive and slow.
detail.solution: Built a full-stack AI platform with a Flask API backend, integrating LiteLLM and RAG (FAISS/Qdrant) to retrieve relevant prior art and case context, generate accurate drafts, and allow iterative refinement.
features: LiteLLM integration with OpenAI fine-tuning and Gemini API
RAG pipeline using FAISS and Qdrant vector stores
Asynchronous task execution with Celery and Redis
Deployed on AWS (EC2, RDS, Lambda, S3)
detail.challenges: Getting the RAG pipeline to surface truly relevant patent documents — not just keyword matches — required careful chunking strategies, embedding model selection, and prompt engineering.
detail.outcome: Deployed to production, handling patent drafting workflows at scale for Dolcera's clients.
